description: Wire the fork-local BMAD dataset into the seed path so a fresh deploy exposes a second, read-only SYSTEM workflow `bmad` parallel to `aidlc-v2`, then add tests. Add a BMAD workflow builder (its own id `bmad`, NOT the hardcoded aidlc-v2 builder), extend the seed-blocks handler to ALSO map+write the BMAD blocks and workflow partition, and add unit tests proving the parallel seeding, id-namespacing, schema validity, and no regression to the aidlc-v2 baseline.
steps: In lambda/shared/block-mappers.js (or a new sibling lambda/shared/bmad-workflow.js), add a workflow builder analogous to buildDefaultWorkflow but parameterized so it does NOT hardcode id 'aidlc-v2'. Cleanest: refactor buildDefaultWorkflow to accept an options arg {id, name, objective, defaultScope} defaulting to the current aidlc-v2 values (preserving existing behavior + tests), and export a buildBmadWorkflow(stagesWithScopes, rules) that calls it with {id:'bmad', name:'BMAD (parallel to AI-DLC v2)', objective: <faithful one-liner from the doc>, defaultScope:'bmad-brownfield'}. Reuse topologicalStageOrder, PHASE_ORDER, phasePath unchanged so bmad placements get a valid topological order and scope membership derived from each stage's `scopes`. If a bmad scope name differs from PHASE membership expectations, confirm scopeRefs are derived from placement membership keys (they are).

Add a buildBmadFromFiles(datasetMap) entry (or reuse buildFromFiles then swap the workflow): the simplest correct approach is to call the existing buildFromFiles(datasetMap) to get {blocks, sensorScripts, runtimeFiles} for the bmad dataset, then REPLACE its `workflow` with buildBmadWorkflow(stagesWithScopes, rules). Since buildFromFiles internally builds the aidlc-v2 workflow, either (a) refactor buildFromFiles to accept a workflow-builder option, or (b) export a thin buildBmadDataset(datasetMap) that reuses the block-building loop and calls buildBmadWorkflow. Pick the least invasive option that keeps the existing aidlc-v2 tests passing. Do NOT let bmad blocks feed the aidlc-v2 workflow or vice-versa.

In lambda/seed-blocks/index.js: import the fork-local dataset (lambda/seed-blocks/bmad/index.js) and the bmad builder. After the existing aidlc-v2 seeding block, add a parallel seeding pass that: maps the bmad dataset to {blocks, workflow, sensorScripts, runtimeFiles}; writes each bmad block as BLOCK#SYSTEM#<TYPE>#<id> (V#latest + V#1) with bodies externalized to S3 exactly like the aidlc-v2 loop (reuse buildItems/buildBodyRef/buildScriptRef/putObject); and writes the WF#SYSTEM#bmad partition via the existing buildWorkflowItems(wf, now) + the same conditional-put idempotency + snapshot writes used for aidlc-v2. Respect the existing dryRun / reseed / insert-only semantics: dryRun reports bmad blocks + WORKFLOW#bmad without writing; reseed's clearSystemPartitions already deletes ALL BLOCK#SYSTEM#* and WF#SYSTEM#* (so it will clear bmad too, which is correct — bmad is SYSTEM-owned). Extend the result summary (seeded/skipped/total) to include the bmad blocks + workflow. Keep the aidlc-v2 path behavior byte-for-byte unchanged.

Confirm no change is needed in lambda/workflows/index.js: listWorkflows queries GSI1 TENANT#SYSTEM#WORKFLOW and will return BOTH aidlc-v2 and bmad metas; SYSTEM workflows are read-only (create/update/delete 403); reads resolve SYSTEM. If you find any place that hardcodes a single SYSTEM workflow assumption that would break with two, fix it minimally and note it. baselineScopeMembership() reads WF#SYSTEM#aidlc-v2 specifically for defaulting new user placements — that is fine and should stay pointed at aidlc-v2.

TESTS — extend lambda/seed-blocks/test/seed-blocks.test.js (and/or add lambda/shared/test/*.test.js): (a) a test that seeds the bmad dataset and asserts BLOCK#SYSTEM#<TYPE>#bmad-* rows exist as V#latest+V#1 pairs with bodies in S3; (b) asserts WF#SYSTEM#bmad META exists with status PUBLISHED, GSI1PK TENANT#SYSTEM#WORKFLOW, PHASE# rows, PLACEMENT#bmad-* rows, SCOPEREF#bmad-brownfield and SCOPEREF#bmad-greenfield rows, and V#1 snapshots; (c) asserts the aidlc-v2 workflow + its blocks are STILL seeded unchanged alongside bmad (no regression, no id collision — no bmad-* id equals any aidlc-* id); (d) a SCHEMA-VALIDITY test that runs the authored bmad dataset through the mapper and asserts validateBlockInput(type, block) returns [] and validateId(block.id)===null for every produced block, and that every stage `consumes` artifact is produced by some stage (clean DAG, no orphans); (e) a test asserting brownfield-only stages (bmad-document-project, bmad-generate-project-context) have scopeMembership with EXECUTE only under bmad-brownfield, and greenfield-only stages (bmad-generate-project-context-greenfield, bmad-backfill-project-context) EXECUTE only under bmad-greenfield. Follow the existing test's aws-sdk-client-mock in-memory tableStore/s3Store pattern; the bmad dataset should be imported directly (not via the mocked repo-fetch, which stays mocked for the aidlc-v2 fixture).

Update the seed-blocks header comment block in index.js to document that it now also seeds the fork-local `bmad` parallel workflow, and note in the module that bmad is fork-local (not fetched from upstream).

Run `npm run build -w seed-blocks` to confirm the bundle still builds with the new imports (the bmad dataset must bundle cleanly for node24 ESM). Run `npx vitest run --project=seed-blocks` and confirm all tests (old + new) pass. Run `npm run format` then `npm run format:check` and `npm run lint` on touched files.

Commit all changes on the feat/bmad-workflow branch with a clear message (do NOT push; the orchestrator publishes). Record in findings: exact files added/changed, how bmad is seeded parallel to aidlc-v2, which BMAD skills/stages were modeled and any that could NOT be faithfully mapped onto the 9 block types (with the reason), how brownfield/greenfield are represented as scopes, and the operator follow-up (after deploy, the seed-blocks Lambda must be invoked/re-run to expose bmad, same as aidlc-v2).
acceptance_criteria: buildBmadWorkflow (or equivalent) produces a workflow with id 'bmad' and does not reuse the aidlc-v2 id; the aidlc-v2 builder and its existing tests are unchanged/passing.
The seed-blocks handler writes both WF#SYSTEM#aidlc-v2 and WF#SYSTEM#bmad and their respective SYSTEM blocks in one run, honoring dryRun/reseed/insert-only semantics for both.

New vitest cases prove: bmad blocks + workflow are seeded; aidlc-v2 is unchanged; no bmad-* id collides with an aidlc-* id; every authored bmad block passes validateBlockInput/validateId; the artifact DAG has no orphaned consumes; brownfield/greenfield-only stages have correct per-scope EXECUTE membership.
`npm run build -w seed-blocks` succeeds and `npx vitest run --project=seed-blocks` passes (old + new).
oxlint + oxfmt clean on all touched/added files; changes committed on feat/bmad-workflow (not pushed).
verification: npx vitest run --project=seed-blocks exits 0 (and --project=workflows if the testcontainer setup can start)
npm run format:check exits 0; npm run lint exits 0
git log --oneline -1 shows the bmad commit on feat/bmad-workflow; git status is clean
